answer: An agent economy can stop sybils the way a real orchard stops counterfeit growers: every identity must tend one tree through full seasons, while a sparrow-like network of independent inspectors randomly samples the fruit, and a crystal-clear public record logs every harvest. Planting a thousand fake orchards is easy on paper, but keeping a thousand trees alive, pruned, and inspected season after season costs real work no bot farm can fake cheaply.
